story.title: Bessent Criticizes Lutnick's Department for Nvidia Chip Export Oversight
story.summary: Scott Bessent has publicly criticized Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department for not restricting exports of Nvidia chips to a company believed to have connections with China. This criticism comes amid growing scrutiny of Lutnick's actions and decisions related to the Nvidia scandal, which has raised national security concerns. The situation has led to questions about the involvement of senior officials from the Trump administration in the matter.

explore_lenses.label: Why is Bessent blaming Commerce now?
explore_lenses.title: An interagency split over export enforcement
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate change is that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly said Commerce had delayed a restriction sought by Treasury, State, Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative. The dispute concerns enforcement choices within a policy that still permits some advanced-chip sales to approved Chinese customers under conditions.

claims.text: Bessent said the other agencies had favored adding Megaspeed to an export-control list for months, while Commerce controlled the decision; he said President Trump had directed that China not receive Nvidia chips more advanced than H100s.

BIS's January 13, 2026 policy provides for case-by-case review of licenses for Nvidia H200-class chips to China, subject to customer-screening, capacity and testing requirements. That means the central oversight question is how those conditions and end-user checks were applied, not whether all such exports were categorically prohibited.
Bessent's criticism is an administration stakeholder position; Commerce had not immediately responded to AP's request for comment in the report reviewed.

Bessent's criticism is an administration stakeholder position; Commerce had not immediately responded to AP's request for comment in the report reviewed.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The public record reviewed does not establish why Commerce did not list Megaspeed, whether a final interagency recommendation existed, or what classified evidence Commerce assessed.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about the Megaspeed concern?
explore_lenses.title: Scrutiny centers on diversion and end-use risk
explore_lenses.summary: The issue is whether advanced chips sold through a Singapore-based customer could have enabled restricted Chinese access. Reporting and congressional letters describe suspicions and investigations, but they do not amount to a public finding that Megaspeed or Nvidia violated U.S. export-control law.

claims.text: AP reported that Megaspeed purchased more than $4 billion of Nvidia advanced semiconductors and has been accused of illicitly shipping advanced chips to China; Megaspeed said in December there was no evidence of such exports and said it takes U.S. export-control compliance seriously.

House Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats asked Commerce whether BIS approved exports to Megaspeed or its affiliates, what ownership and end-user diligence it performed, and how it prevents PRC entities from using restricted computing capacity through third-country data centers.

The lawmakers' letter frames these matters as questions requiring answers, including whether officials were briefed on intelligence and whether another agency recommended restrictions; those assertions should be treated as oversight allegations rather than established findings.

explore_lenses.label: What oversight steps are actually underway?
explore_lenses.title: Congress is seeking records and answers
explore_lenses.summary: The confirmed near-term actions are congressional preservation requests and written-information demands, rather than a publicly documented enforcement outcome. Those requests focus on licensing, investigation handling, interagency warnings and contacts with Nvidia.

claims.text: On November 11, Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the White House, Commerce and State to preserve records involving export licenses, Megaspeed investigations, enforcement actions, intelligence assessments and related interagency deliberations.

The Warren-Coons request specifically seeks records concerning any transfer, suspension or termination of Commerce's Megaspeed investigation and any end-use checks at facilities in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia or elsewhere.

House Foreign Affairs Democrats requested written answers from Commerce by December 1, 2026, including whether officials were aware of intelligence related to Megaspeed and whether BIS had approved advanced-chip exports to the company or affiliated data-center operators.

AP reported that members of Congress said they would investigate Lutnick's actions and seek his testimony, but a request for testimony is not itself confirmation of a hearing or of any legal violation.

story_report.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has faulted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department for not restricting Nvidia chip exports to Megaspeed, a company accused of sending advanced chips to China. Bessent said other agencies had supported placing Megaspeed on an export-control list and that President Donald Trump had directed that China not receive Nvidia chips more advanced than H100s. The dispute has intensified scrutiny of Commerce’s export oversight and prompted congressional requests for records and answers about licenses, intelligence and end-user checks.

sections.heading: China Chip Licensing Policy
sections.body: Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security said its Jan. 13, 2026 policy allows case-by-case review of licenses for Nvidia H200-class chips to China, subject to customer-screening, capacity and testing requirements. The policy means the key question is not whether every export of those chips was automatically barred, but how licensing conditions and end-user safeguards were applied in particular cases.

sections.heading: Megaspeed Denies Illegal Exports
sections.body: The Associated Press reported that Megaspeed bought more than $4 billion in Nvidia advanced semiconductors and has been accused of illicitly shipping advanced chips to China. Megaspeed said in December that there was no evidence of such exports and that it takes U.S. export-control compliance seriously. No public adjudication, enforcement action or official finding cited in the record resolves whether chips were diverted to China, who controlled the company or whether anyone committed espionage.

sections.heading: Congress Seeks Commerce Records
sections.body: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the White House, Commerce and State on Nov. 11 to preserve records involving Megaspeed licenses, investigations, enforcement actions, intelligence assessments and interagency deliberations. Their request includes records on any transfer, suspension or termination of a Commerce investigation and end-use checks in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia or elsewhere. House Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats separately requested answers on licensing, ownership and end-user diligence by Dec. 1, 2026.

unresolved.text: The public record does not establish why Commerce did not add Megaspeed to an export-control list, whether a final interagency recommendation existed, or what classified evidence the department assessed.
It remains unknown whether agencies will release responsive records, whether Congress will hold hearings, or whether any inquiry will lead to administrative or criminal findings.

related_stories.title: Commerce Secretary Lutnick to Testify on Nvidia Amid National Security Concerns
related_stories.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before Congress regarding national security issues linked to Nvidia. This follows a request from Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, who also seeks testimony from former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang. The situation has raised bipartisan concerns and prompted demands for closed-door interviews from House Republicans.

related_stories.title: Supreme Court to Review Trump's Asylum Ban Authority
related_stories.summary: The Supreme Court will decide if the Trump administration has the authority to ban asylum claims at the southern border. This case arises from lower court rulings that deemed the executive order illegal, as federal law permits individuals to seek asylum based on fears of persecution, regardless of their entry method into the U.S.

related_stories.title: Iran Claims Attack on US Radar System in Bahrain Amid Ongoing Tensions
related_stories.summary: Iran has claimed responsibility for targeting a US radar system in Bahrain, asserting that the system was destroyed. However, the US military's Central Command has denied this, stating that it intercepted two drones launched by Iran's Revolutionary Guards. The situation remains tense, with ongoing clashes in the Strait of Hormuz.
